subject: Payment cadence & temporary credit holdback request
messages:
From: Ella Simmons <ella.simmons@acmelogistics.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@acmelogistics.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary payment terms & security holdback

Hi David / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the throughput and the routing controls. We have one outstanding billing ask from Acme Finance: because of a seasonal cashflow peak, we need to request temporary term flexibility for the first quarter of the contract.

Specifically:
- Request: Net60 on invoices for the first 3 billing cycles (Nov–Jan)
- Credit limit cap: we would like a soft cap at $120,000 per month while we finish our internal approval
- Security holdback: Finance would be open to a one-month security deposit (refundable after 90 days) if that helps with credit exposure

We also need clear VAT/evidence handling — please confirm that Redwood can supply VAT-registered invoices and that you can provide VAT receipts for the EU subsidiary if required.

I attached our Q4 forecast and the PO we plan to send (Acme_PO_4532.pdf).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) accept Net60 temporarily, (b) hold a security deposit, and (c) provide VAT documentation? If not Net60, what is the best alternative?

Best,
Ella Simmons
VP Finance, Acme Logistics

Attachments: Q4-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet), Acme_PO_4532.pdf (purchase order)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Simmons <ella.simmons@acmelogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 13:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary payment terms & security holdback

Hi Ella — thanks for outlining this so clearly. We can be flexible for pilots and seasonal peaks; below is a proposed compromise that balances Acme's cashflow needs and Redwood's credit risk controls.

Proposal (temporary, first 90 days):
- Term: Net45 standard, but approve Net60 for the first 3 invoices as a one-time pilot conditional on the following controls.
- Credit buffer: Redwood will provision a temporary credit buffer of $150,000 against the account for the 90-day period.
- Security holdback: rather than a full one-month invoice deposit, we propose a refundable holdback equal to 25% of the first invoice (applied as a credit against subsequent invoices). This reduces initial exposure while lowering Acme's upfront cash requirement.
- Staged invoicing option: if Acme prefers, we can accept a 50/50 split on the first invoice (50% upon delivery, 50% net45) — see attached sample-payment-plan.csv for two variants.

VAT and tax evidence:
- We will provide VAT-registered invoices and can attach VAT receipts for EU entities; please send your VAT registration number and the legal entity you want invoiced.

Next steps:
1) If this looks OK, sign the attached credit-application.pdf and return the signed PO (or DocuSign link below).
2) We'll provision the credit buffer and set the temporary Net60 flag in the billing system.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/12345-ACME-PO-4532

If you want to firm the wording we can convert this to a short amendment to the SOW — Marissa, can you help with the amendment language if Acme accepts?

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit-application.pdf (form), sample-payment-plan.csv (CSV)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary payment terms & security holdback

Vivek — looping you in for quick approval on the temporary credit buffer and the proposed holdback structure for Acme (deal ACME-2026-09-INV-741). Short summary: Acme asked for Net60 for first 3 cycles; David proposed Net45 default + Net60 pilot, $150k temporary buffer, and 25% refundable holdback vs 1-month deposit.

Questions for you:
- Approve temporary $150k credit buffer?
- OK to accept 25% refundable holdback instead of 100% month deposit?
- Approve us creating a short SOW amendment reflecting staged payment plan if Acme picks the 50/50 option?

HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5421/ACME-2026-09-INV-741

If you approve, I will send the DocuSign and update finance with the temporary limit.

— Marissa
Director, Commercial Ops

On Wed, Nov 4, 2026 at 1:48 PM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> [included above]

From: Ella Simmons <ella.simmons@acmelogistics.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, accounts-payable@acmelogistics.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary payment terms & security holdback

Thanks David — that approach should work for us with a few tweaks. We discussed internally and propose the following final cadence for the trial period:

- Invoice 1 (upon delivery): 30% due immediately; 30% due at 30 days; remaining 40% at 60 days.
- Temporary credit buffer: we accept the $150k buffer.
- Security holdback: reduced to 20% of Invoice 1 (refundable after 90 days).
- VAT documentation: attached is Acme's VAT certificate for the invoiced entity (vat-registration.pdf) and we attached the signed PO (signed-PO_4532.pdf). Please ensure VAT invoices reference our EU VAT ID.

Please confirm the agreed plan and send back the short amendment or DocuSign link. Also add our AP contact (accounts-payable@acmelogistics.com) as the billing recipient going forward.

Best regards,
Ella Simmons
VP Finance, Acme Logistics

Attachments: signed-PO_4532.pdf (signed purchase order), vat-registration.pdf (VAT certificate)
